html:
In late April 2007 Estonia moved a Soviet war memorial, the Bronze Soldier, from central Tallinn. Riots by Russian speakers followed, and for weeks waves of cyberattacks hit Estonian banks, media and government websites.

To many ethnic Estonians the statue stood for Soviet occupation; to many of the large Russian-speaking minority it honoured the victory over Nazism. The riots of the Bronze Night left one dead. The attacks used huge networks of hijacked computers. Estonia blamed Russia, which denied it.

It was the first time a whole country was attacked this way, and it was especially serious for a state as dependent on the internet as Estonia with e-Estonia. NATO opened its cyber defence centre in Tallinn in 2008, and the event shaped later rules on cyber war.
